notes.title: A Quick but Notable Update
notes.content:
Rusty Flesh's demo has just been updated with the following changes:

[list]
[*] Projectiles now render over other sprites.
[*] ​Added controller support to the PC version (Steam) thanks to the [url=https://eastpixel.itch.io/gbcbag]GBCBag 2[/url] tool by Chris at EASTPIXEL​.

In addition, I'm not planning to keep updating the demo until after the full game launches, unless new critical bugs are discovered. I need to focus on finishing the game, and with this, the demo should be polished enough to grant an enjoyable experience.

​Thank you for your understanding!

notes.title: Progress Report and Roadmap
notes.content:
Hello!

The development of Rusty Flesh is going well lately. [b]Three fully playable areas[/b] (plus the initial "Storehouse" area that works as a tutorial) [b]are ready[/b], and the fourth and final one is under development as I write these lines. And even better: these three areas are interconnected, can be explored in any order, and feel good to play.

[h2]Chambers[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/72b6c0e939d213399aeeb788f7822d6e49b351c2.png[/img]

This is the first area that was made, and the one you can play in the demo after the Storehouse. It's like a sidescrolling Sokoban, where you push crates to complete the puzzles.

[h2]Engines[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/d459190e6b458b17c03509b87f5c91cee5cb35ed.png[/img]

This area is hot! So, it is really dangerous to explore without the right equipment. Still, everything's possible. Here, you'll find fire, robots and teleporters. Don't get lost!

[h2]Greenhouse[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/2369cf0bc10cfb551fc5d9018cbfef3622ce2d31.png[/img]

Turn lights on and off, and connect circuits to progress through this area. Light and darkness hide different secrets, so be very aware of your surroundings.

So, what's next?

Right now, [b]I'm working on the final area, the Control Bridge[/b]. which is unlocked only after completing the three previous ones. There will be of course a final boss, and the story will unfold.

I also need to design and make the [b]vents system[/b]. It will be a top-down maze connecting different areas of the game, allowing for shortcuts and hiding its own secrets.

After that, I'll make an in-game [b]achievements system[/b], just for fun. And, obviously, cutscenes for the different endings, credits and lots of testing and polishing.

Last but not least, I already have a [b]launch date[/b] in mind! Stay tuned, I'll upload a new trailer and reveal the launch date as soon as possible.

notes.title: Demo Update: Ready for Steam Next Fest!
notes.content:
Hi, it's definitely been a while! But no worries, I've been working hard on Rusty Flesh, and I'll have some exciting news [i]very[/i] soon.

But meanwhile, the demo build has been updated with the following changes:

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug that made the pause and map screens unavailable.
[*] Improved acceleration and deceleration responsiveness.
[*] Undead soldiers (green uniform) now revive faster after stunning them.
[/list]

Not much, huh? But the game does feel much better now after these simple improvements, and [b]Rusty Flesh's demo is ready for the February 2025 edition of Steam Next Fest![/b] This means that there will be no better time to try it and wishlist it than February 24 - March 3.

See you soon!

notes.title: How to play Rusty Flesh on Steam Deck (and notes on how to play on PC)
notes.content:
[b]IMPORTANT NOTE: The steps outlined below are not longer relevant, as Steam Decks and controllers are supported now, but this post will not be deleted, just in case somebody finds it useful.[/b]

Rusty Flesh is made with GB Studio, an engine specifically tailored to create Game Boy games that doesn't support PC builds natively, let alone Steam Deck compatibility. [b]The good news is that you can just download a custom layout, and it feels great![/b] And of course, you can always create your own. It's easier than it sounds.

As Rusty Flesh is made for the Game Boy Color, its native controles are just a D-pad, A, B, Start and Select. For the PC version, they are mapped as follows:
[list]
[*]D-pad (Game Boy): arrow keys (PC)
[*]A (Game Boy): Z (PC)
[*]B (Game Boy): X (PC)
[*]Start (Game Boy): Enter (PC)
[*]Select (Game Boy): Shift (PC)
[/list]
When it comes to Steam Deck, this is how you can play the game (and the demo):
[olist]
[*]On your Deck, click the little controller icon on the right side of the screen.[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/c793107017790d2e2a5345c29216002c610f76f5.jpg[/img]
[*]On the top of the screen, click on your current layout.[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/a819b43e93aa1ed1e836ee3f972ca9e3720b8eb1.jpg[/img]
[*]Go to the Community Layouts tab, and choose any of the "Retro Game Boy templates" you'll see. They're all the same, I just messed it up when uploading it. [i](Note: If you can't see any templates, press X on your Deck and you should see all the community templates.)[/i][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/353ae84cb5345f11a41059c367bb88e2d61f37af.jpg[/img]
[*]You will see this screen. As you can see, only the D-pad and A, B, X, Y are available (similar to a Game Boy's D-pad and A, B, Start and Select buttons). This is to keep that retro feeling, even in modern hardware. Download and apply this template, and you can start playing![img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/851c4dcab62d6dcd522157c5f2f8d3a444e71e82.jpg[/img]
[/olist]
But what if you don't like my retro template? If that's the case, creating your own couldn't be easier.
[olist]
[*]First, go to the Templates tab, and scroll down until you find "Keyboard (WASD) and Mouse".[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/91811debb46a6de9e58a1d69f37818ee79b8a4d7.jpg[/img]
[*]Click on it, and on the screen you'll see, click on the Steam Deck controls you want to use and select a keyboard's arrow keys, Z, X, Enter and Shift to map them accordingly. Save and apply, and you're all set! [i](Note: You can optionally disable the controls you're not using.)[/i][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45028137/67f5422b7f9fa47dae428a9214f41c68466030e1.jpg[/img]
[/olist]
Comment if you have any questions, and enjoy!

notes.title: Demo Update: New Splash Screen and more
notes.content:
Hello everyone, and happy spooky season!

I've been wanting to update Rusty Flesh's demo for a while now, and finally, here it is! This is what has changed:

[list]
[*] Fixed a bug that prevented players from correctly switching gravity when standing on an object (platforms, boxes...).
[*] Created a new splash screen.
[*] Fixed some minor narrative inconsistencies.
[*] Some minor graphic improvements.
[/list]

Also, the Engines area is [i]almost[/i] ready, and I'm working on releasing a new trailer soon! I'll keep you posted. Oh, and remember that to wishlist Rusty Flesh!

notes.title: Demo Update: Improvements, Bug Fixes and New Content
notes.content:
Howdy!

It's been a while, but I'm back with some updates. I actually wanted to update the demo a while ago, but some of the bug fixes I implemented created new, bigger bugs, I wasn't satisfied with how certain puzzles felt, and so on. Anyway, Rusty Flesh demo has been finally updated, and here's a list of the changes:

[list]
[*] Modified a room where it was impossible to go back without dying.
[*] Slightly increased the difficulty of two puzzles that were reported to be way too easy.
[*] Added a small section of the vents area (a top-down area that will serve as a shortcut between different places and hide some secrets).
[*] Fixed a transition between rooms that sent the player to a wrong place.
[*] Fixed a bug where you could die when walking from a moving platform.
[/list]

Hope you enjoy it! I'll keep working on the Engines area, and hopefully I will have something to show soon.

Thank you for playing!
